scope: Historical exact-path WordPress page-cache supplement from the original account archive; not a current served page, live listing inventory, target equivalence or redirect approval

r07-rendered-cache-review.html.content: Escaped script-free text, historical canonical and listing links from each exact-path cached file

r07-rendered-cache-index.csv.content: Private URL spelling, cached file kind and hash, title, heading and link-count index

r07-rendered-cache-private.json.content: Private exact archive-member and frozen URL mapping for each cache candidate

r07-rendered-cache-manifest.json.content: Private output counts and review-file hashes

r07-extract-rendered-cache.py.content: Private extractor requiring the original archive, nested homedir index and frozen source match report

r07-build-rendered-review.py.content: Private script-free review builder requiring the extracted cache and frozen source match report

limitations: Twenty-three files are named _index.html.old; the other four may also be stale. The archive does not prove when or whether these bytes were served to any visitor.
The four cached transfer spellings have no exact published WordPress post record in the restored database; cache text is historical source evidence, not publication authority.
The two .ru root spellings are one identity and one cached file. Historical root and listing archive card sets differ; neither justifies treating either route as a redirect.
The 61 missing exact-path cache spellings still require source reconstruction or explicit human decisions; an absent cache file is not proof that a page did not exist.
Cached HTML may contain old or inaccurate facts and active third-party scripts. Only the escaped script-free private review view is intended for human inspection.
No current target content, photo rights, status, locale or URL equivalence was reviewed; the original URL decision form remains unsigned.
